part: Treasure Chess sky panoramas: Whitby in academic realism
note: Whitby redone in academic realism (crisp, finished detail) for the Shipyard's painted sky. Claude, 25 Nov 2026.
style: One single wide, highly finished academic-realist oil painting, nineteenth-century salon quality: precise drawing, crisp architectural detail, smooth glazed paint with only fine brushwork, true perspective and atmosphere. Seen from far out at sea; the horizon low in the frame and perfectly level. No ships, no boats, no people; no text, lettering, signature, monogram, border or black bars.

beats.text: Whitby on the Yorkshire coast in late-afternoon light, painted in the manner of Edward William Cooke and Ivan Aivazovsky: the ruined Gothic abbey on the East Cliff drawn stone by stone, St Mary's Church with its churchyard of leaning gravestones beside it at the cliff top, the old town's red pantile roofs and whitewashed walls stepping down to the harbour, the two stone harbour piers on their rock outcrops with their white lighthouses; the whole town occupies only the left quarter of the picture and sits small in the distance. Open sea fills the rest under towering golden cumulus and a deep blue sky; calm deep-blue water with long gentle swell.

Whitby on the Yorkshire coast at night in a gale, painted in the manner of Ivan Aivazovsky and John Atkinson Grimshaw: the ruined Gothic abbey and St Mary's Church with its churchyard dark against a moonlit sky on the East Cliff, warm gaslit windows in the old town below, the stone harbour pier on its rock outcrop with the lighthouse lit; the town occupies only the left quarter of the picture and sits small in the distance. Heavy storm clouds with the moon breaking through, rough sea with breaking waves and moonlit spray filling the rest.
